title: Operator-Level Quantum-Classical Correspondence in Relativistic Quantum Theory and Curved Spacetime
authors: Pankaj Sheoran, Gopal Kashyap, Sanjay Siwach
abstract: In a recent work \cite{Shaikh:2026nsi}, it was shown that for a non-relativistic particle, the operator equations of motion can be cast in the same differential form as Newton's equation of motion. This establishes a correspondence between quantum operator dynamics and classical mechanics at the level of the equations of motion. In this work, we investigate whether this correspondence extends to quantum field theory and linearized gravity. We explicitly show that the Heisenberg equations of motion for quantum field operators reproduce the corresponding classical equations of motion for a broad class of field theories. The Klein-Gordon equation, Maxwell's equations, Yang-Mills equations, and linearized Einstein equations are shown to arise at the operator level without taking the limit $\hbar\rightarrow0$. We then extend the analysis to curved spacetime and show that the quantum field operators satisfy the corresponding covariant field equations at the operator level. In the weak-field approximation, we show that the Heisenberg evolution of the metric-perturbations reproduces the linearized Einstein equations at the operator level. For a quantum particle in curved spacetime, the Heisenberg equations for position and momentum reproduce classical geodesic motion in the semiclassical limit, thereby extending the operator-level quantum-classical correspondence from fields to particle dynamics.
summary: This work rigorously examines the quantum-classical correspondence by analyzing the Heisenberg equations of motion for various quantum systems, including fields and particles, in curved spacetime. It demonstrates that the quantum evolution equations naturally reproduce the corresponding classical field equations and geodesic motion at the operator level. This establishes a powerful, systematic framework for understanding semiclassical physics in curved backgrounds.
main_problem: The paper investigates the extent to which the quantum-classical correspondence, established for non-relativistic particles, holds true when extended to quantum field theory and curved spacetime.
main_result: The Heisenberg equations of motion for quantum fields and particles reproduce the corresponding classical field equations (like Maxwell's or Einstein's) and geodesic motion at the operator level, even without taking the $\hbar 	o 0$ limit for the core dynamics.
method: The primary method involves using the Heisenberg picture formalism to derive equations of motion directly from the quantum operators, comparing these results systematically against known classical equations.
model_or_system: The analysis covers several systems: free and interacting scalar and Dirac fields in flat and curved spacetime, electromagnetic fields, and the dynamics of a quantum test particle in a curved background.
key_observables:
Heisenberg equations of motion for field operators ($\hat{\phi}, \hat{\psi}$), metric perturbations ($\hat{h}_{\mu
u}$), and the position/momentum operators ($\hat{x}_\mu, \hat{p}_\mu$).
important_parameters:
Curvature-coupling parameter ($\xi$), Planck's constant ($\hbar$), and the background metric tensor ($g_{\mu
u}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Heisenberg picture formalism and employs the semiclassical approximation when linking quantum matter fields to the classical background metric in gravity.
paper_structure: The paper builds systematically: first establishing the correspondence for non-relativistic particles, then extending it to free and interacting quantum fields in flat spacetime (QFT), and finally generalizing the framework to curved spacetime for fields and test particles.
why_interesting: While the focus is on QFT and gravity, the rigorous demonstration of operator-level correspondence provides a powerful, systematic tool for analyzing quantum dynamics in complex backgrounds, which is foundational for understanding quantum gravity effects.
